name: Lunar Polar Water-Ice Prospecting Sprint v1
description: A short-horizon, prospecting-only benchmark on the anchor's Shackleton-de Gerlache world (scenarios/1-lunar-polar-ice-prospecting.md): in a single 7-day surface campaign a relay orbiter, a cargo lander, and an active-perception scout must characterize the permanently shadowed regions and localize water ice under power and comms-window constraints - no excavation or ISRU. A distinct task from the 30-day anchor: it scores only the belief/discovery metrics, ranks by information gain, and is bounded by a wall-clock + compute budget. Content is REUSED by hash from the anchor's published Hub artifacts (RM-P1-WORLDS-15 / RM-P1-FLEET-10 / RM-P1-PROSPECT-13) - see PROVENANCE.md; reusing the same content under a new task is exactly how the zoo grows without republishing (bench.md §8). This scenario does not exercise the operational_targeting dual-use gate.

world.description: Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge, lunar south pole, version 0.4.0 - ships its horizon map, so the world resolves in ~3 s instead of re-deriving a 192-million-entry skyline from the packaged DEM on every load (astro-mine-worlds#46). Terrain and regolith rasters are byte-identical to the prior bundle; the PSR mask is now the spec-driven, validated one (|error| 0.0400 inside the 0.0500 budget, where the 0.1.0 world this pinned before was at 0.0586 - outside it).
